stops.note: origin disputed (traditionally Latin avia 'grandmother', though some link it to a Gothic word for 'guardian'); Portuguese households in Goa, taken by Afonso de Albuquerque in 1510, gave the word to local nursemaids
British families in India hired ayahs and often brought them on the voyage home; London's Ayahs' Home (at Hackney from 1900) sheltered those left stranded

current_meaning: a nursemaid or maid in South Asia
